character_sheet: A tameable, rideable ostrich: a two-block body with a rump and an under-tail block, a 21-tall neck to a skull with an upper and a lower beak, three zero-thickness tail plumes, two stub wings, and two legs of a hip, a thigh, a shin and a four-plate foot with four zero-thickness claws (OstrichModel.java:107-295, 38 parts; the two hat pieces stay hidden, :412-413). 25 HP, speed 0.38 and an unused attack of 6 - it has no attack goal (Ostrich.java:125-144). It flees monsters within 8 blocks, panics when hurt, is tempted by wheat and tamed by it one time in two (:130-132, :160-174); an empty hand mounts it, tame or wild (:176-182, :204-215), and the rider drives a client-predicted sprint with a throttle to 0.75, a 1.85 yaw lag and a 'FAST' hop on the jump key (:49-71, :237-243); it takes no fall damage (:289-292) and shrugs off cactus (:146-154). It spawns in daylight above y 50 on a 1-in-4 roll, no other within 16 (:302-310; ModEntities.java:555-556). Read it as an ostrich: long strides that snap to a kick at speed, the plumes waving, an occasional wing flap, the head leaning into a ridden turn.
size_notes: Drawn at x1.0 of the rig (OstrichRenderer.java:23; shadow 0.55, :25; no baby scale in the port renderer) on a 256x128 sheet (OstrichModel.java:297), ostrich.png (OstrichRenderer.java:19); the hitbox is 0.85 x 2.1 (ModEntities.java:555-556). The original's ModelOstrich(0.65f) argument was the wingspeed (OstrichModel.java:22), not a scale. Hat1 and Hat2 are never visible (getIsActivated is a constant 0, Ostrich.java:116-117; OstrichModel.java:412-413).

groups.name: gait
groups.amplitude: pi x 0.4 x the TRUE horizontal speed in blocks per tick (from xOld / zOld, not limbSwingAmount), and snapped to ±0.75 rad (43 deg) whenever it passes ±0.5 rad - a kick plateau at a run; every piece of a leg by the same angle about its rest (hip -0.297, thigh 0.483, shin -0.437, foot and claws 0), the right the negative; no threshold
groups.plain: the two legs stride fore and aft as stiff chains, opposite each other, the swing growing with the real speed and snapping to a fixed kick when it runs
groups.math: s = sqrt((xOld - x)^2 + (zOld - z)^2); a = cos(t * 1.25 * 0.65) * pi * s * 0.4; a = a > 0.5 ? 0.75 : a < -0.5 ? -0.75 : a; leftleg.xRot = -0.297 + a; LLeg1.xRot = 0.483 + a; LLeg2.xRot = -0.437 + a; Lfoot1..4.xRot = LClaw1..4.xRot = a; the right leg: rest - a
groups.phase: the amplitude is the entity's real speed, so the reference clip's fixed limbSwingAmount does not drive it
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 1.25 x 0.65 = 0.8125: the natural period is 7.73 ticks

groups.name: tail
groups.axis: x (all three) and y (the side plumes)
groups.amplitude: pitch: pi x 0.06 = 0.188 rad (11 deg) about -0.594 at 0.05 rad/tick, all three plumes together; yaw: pi x 0.08 = 0.251 rad (14 deg) about -0.334 for the left plume at 0.061 rad/tick and about +0.334 for the right at 0.072 rad/tick
groups.plain: the three tail plumes rise and fall together on a slow wave while the two side plumes fan in and out on their own slower rhythms
groups.math: Tail1.xRot = Tail2.xRot = Tail3.xRot = -0.594 + cos(t * 0.05) * pi * 0.06; Tail3.yRot = -0.334 + cos(t * 0.061) * pi * 0.08; Tail2.yRot = 0.334 - cos(t * 0.072) * pi * 0.08
groups.omega_note: the classic phases are ageInTicks x 0.05 (126 ticks), x 0.061 (103 ticks) and x 0.072 (87 ticks) - no wingspeed term

groups.name: wings
groups.amplitude: pi x 0.15 = 0.471 rad (27 deg), one-sided (the absolute value), the wing yawing half of that; played only when a per-entity latch, rerolled one chance in three at each negative-to-positive zero crossing of the 9.7-tick cycle, is set - else 0
groups.plain: the wings flap out and back in a one-sided beat, one cycle in three on average, still the rest of the time
groups.math: w = cos(t * 1.0 * 0.65) * pi * 0.15; n = cos((t + 0.3) * 1.0 * 0.65) * pi * 0.15; if (n > 0 && w < 0) ri1 = nextInt(3) == 1; if (ri1 == 0) w = 0; w = |w|; Lwing.zRot = -w; Lwing.yRot = w / 2; Rwing.zRot = w; Rwing.yRot = -w / 2
groups.phase: a client-side roll on the per-entity RenderInfo, not a synched state
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 1.0 x 0.65: the natural period is 9.67 ticks; the absolute value halves the visible beat

behaviour: One gait rhythm with no threshold (OstrichModel.java:313-343): the two legs stride as stiff chains at 0.8125 rad/tick (a 7.7-tick period) with an amplitude of pi x 0.4 x the entity's TRUE horizontal speed - read from its last position, not limbSwingAmount - and snapped to ±0.75 rad whenever it passes ±0.5, so a running ostrich kicks to a fixed 43 degrees; every piece of a leg, feet and claws included, takes the same angle, the right leg the negative of the left.

Three unscaled rhythms: the three tail plumes pitch 11 degrees together on a 126-tick wave while the side plumes fan 14 degrees on 103- and 87-tick waves (:344-347); the wings flap 27 degrees one-sided on a 9.7-tick cycle only when a per-entity latch, rerolled one chance in three at each cycle's zero crossing, is set (:389-406).

The head branches three ways. Ridden (:355-365), the head yaw becomes the entity's own turn rate x 20, smoothed at a sixtieth per tick and clamped to ±50 - a lean into the turn; otherwise the look yaw is halved (:366-368). In the sitting pose (:371-377) the skull, both beaks, the neck and the hats flip upside down (xRot pi) with no yaw - though no code path in the port sets the ostrich sitting (mobInteract :157-185 tames and mounts only; mounting clears it :179), so the branch is dormant; else they sit level (:378-384). The skull, beaks and hats then yaw at 0.65 of that head yaw (:385-388); the neck's yaw is not written.
The body blocks, rump and under-tail are static. The ridden run (Ostrich.java:237-243, the RiderFlightController), its FAST hop (:49-58) and the taming are not animation events.

wishlist: in `walk`: the code's stride swings every leg piece by one angle (OstrichModel.java:322-343) — bend the knee and let the foot plates flick; keep the snap to a fixed kick above 0.5 rad (:316-321), it is the ostrich's run
in `idle`: the tail plumes' three slow waves (:344-347) with a head bob and a look-around; the neck is a single 21-tall bone (:252-255), so the bob lives at its base
in `flap`: one full two-sided beat — the code's flap is one-sided (:401) and plays one cycle in three (:396-398)
in `sit`: a real crouch with the legs folded under the body — the code only flips the head (:371-377)
